prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system (continuous potable water, automatic control, manual intervention); boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Aliases: Ironwood=River Intake Pump Station (automatic; start permissives: suction level, discharge path, healthy motor, open valves, no trips; blocked by low channel level, drive fault, local control, unproven interlock; lost permissive→alarm/stop; maintenance release after isolations tagged, verified, logged in shift turnover record). Lantern=SCADA Historian Server (trends, doses, analyzers, filters, washes, lab timestamps, pre/post-work performance). Marigold=Coagulant Dosing Skid (sends Alum Batch Ticket on new lot; analyzer-trimmed dose). Cobalt=North Filter Gallery. Sparrow=Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (sends Jar Test Photograph Set; takes maintenance return samples). Quarry=Maintenance Planner. Elements: Raw Water Screen Channel (sends Rake Torque Snapshot to Maintenance Planner); South Filter Gallery (sends Filter Run Exception Note); Clearwell Level Controller (storage limits; low-level interlock blocks pumps; high-level alarm); Chlorine Contact Basin (maintains contact time); Backwash Recovery Tank; High Service Pump Header; North/South Distribution Pressure Stations. Items: Chlorine Residual Alarm; Sample Chain Slip (Laboratory Technician sends); Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log (Chemical Supplier Driver sends before unloading). Requirements: manual override only when automatic unavailable, reason stated; large feed changes need Chief Operator approval; analyzer loss: hold dose, grab samples; samples labeled at collection, QC before release; Storm Intake Mode increases sampling, re-reviews discretionary work; work orders state window, responsible person, isolations, return condition; lockout all energy; isolation verified by craft, acknowledged by operations; Distribution Dispatcher informed before header/pressure station changes; Chlorine Residual Alarm pauses maintenance task, verify sample flow, compare grab sample, hold production increase; return to service needs evidence and jumpers/bypasses/tools removed; failed test keeps work order open, Chief Operator decides isolate/restrict; disinfection returns to normal after Chief Operator confirms consistency in Lantern; chlorine feed adjusted gradually. Actors: Chief Operator; Duty Engineer (configuration, temporary dose, defers nonessential work); Laboratory Technician (verifies lot, confirms sampling needs, confirmatory residuals); Chemical Supplier Driver; Distribution Dispatcher.

New part:
S134: The Clearwell Level Controller sends the Clearwell Diver Entry Permit when level and isolation prerequisites have been verified by the control system.
S135: Clearwell level changes are trended against filter production and high-service demand so that slow instrumentation errors can be distinguished from actual storage changes.
S136: The High Service Pump Header is identified in voice radio traffic by the alias Juniper when operators need a short confirmation name.
S137: The High Service Pump Header sequences available pumps to meet distribution demand while avoiding unnecessary starts, short cycling, and operation near unstable portions of the pump curves.
S138: Lead and lag pump assignments are rotated according to runtime, availability, and any operating restriction entered by the Chief Operator.
S139: Header pressure control uses a paced response so that pump starts, pump speed changes, and valve movements do not create avoidable pressure transients in the distribution system.
S140: The High Service Pump Header produces the Pump Bearing Vibration Clip after a configured vibration threshold is exceeded during pump operation.
S141: If a high-service pump trips, the remaining available pumps are evaluated automatically against the current pressure setpoint before another unit is started.
S142: The North Distribution Pressure Station and South Distribution Pressure Station receive pressure support through coordinated setpoints that reflect system demand and storage conditions.
S143: The Distribution Dispatcher is identified by the alias Falcon during pressure coordination calls with plant staff.
S144: The Distribution Dispatcher communicates expected demand changes, main break impacts, and pressure complaints so that plant pumping decisions match field conditions.
S145: During Storm Intake Mode, operators watch the relationship between raw water quality, filter loading, disinfectant demand, and high-service pumping to avoid forcing production beyond treatment capability.
S146: Abnormal clearwell level, loss of residual, loss of pump header pressure, or conflicting instrument readings require the Duty Engineer to review the operating condition before setpoints are changed outside normal ranges.
S147: The SCADA Historian Server stores residual, level, pressure, and pump status data at sufficient resolution to support event reconstruction after alarms or customer pressure complaints.
S148: Manual operation is allowed only when the operator can maintain residual targets, clearwell limits, and distribution pressure with direct observation of the affected indications.
S149: Return to automatic control requires stable chlorine residual, stable clearwell level response, and confirmed high-service pressure control for a period set by the Chief Operator.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
